title: ReversingLabs links SSO vishing campaign to new extortion group Inception
date_note: Date of ReversingLabs' blog post; it says the campaign has been active since late October 2026.

key_findings: ReversingLabs says the Inception extortion group listed seven claimed victims on a Tor leak site; it describes these as unverified claims.
It says the group uses voice phishing to steal single sign-on credentials, and its lure domains have no mail DNS records, so they cannot receive email.

ReversingLabs identified 21 confirmed phishing domains running a kit that tailors pages to the target's identity provider, Okta or NetIQ; visitors who are not targets are redirected to the company's legitimate site.
Shared Cloudflare nameservers, NICENIC registrations and evening UTC registration patterns link the infrastructure, and ReversingLabs says they suggest further corporate targets beyond the leak site.
It says the activity has run since late October 2026.
recommendations: Require phishing-resistant authentication such as FIDO2 keys, passkeys or origin-bound authenticators, plus managed device controls and alerts on unexpected MFA changes.
Train employees and help desks to verify urgent legal or compliance sign-in requests, and verify identity before resetting credentials or MFA.
Monitor new domain registrations and certificate transparency logs for brand-plus-legal naming, and block suspicious domains at DNS and web proxies.
Hunt DNS, proxy and identity logs from 21 October 2026 onward; if targeting is confirmed, revoke sessions and reset credentials.

place: United States (no victim location stated; pin at country)
geo_basis: country; the report names no single location
summary: ReversingLabs says a vishing campaign aimed at single sign-on credentials is associated with Inception, a data-extortion group that appeared on a Tor leak site in mid-November 2026. Its seven listed victims are unverified claims. Help Net Security and The Hacker News report that Okta tracks the actors as O-UNC-053 and assesses the cluster changed its brand affiliation.
plain: Security firm ReversingLabs says phone-call scams targeting company single sign-on logins are tied to a new extortion group, Inception. Its seven listed victims are unverified claims.
exec: A new extortion group is reportedly using phone-based phishing against SSO logins; the seven victims it lists are unverified claims.
action: ReversingLabs advises phishing-resistant authentication such as FIDO2 keys or passkeys, verifying identity before credential or MFA resets, and hunting DNS, proxy and identity logs from October 21, 2026 onward.
impact: ReversingLabs says the leak-site listings are unverified claims.

validation.note: ReversingLabs vendor post (primary); Help Net Security and The Hacker News (two publishers) both report Okta's O-UNC-053 tracking name and brand-change assessment; Okta's own page not read.

review.note: Compared date, seven unverified claims, 21 domains, Okta/NetIQ, Inception attribution by ReversingLabs, Okta tracking name via Help Net Security and THN; actor-unsourced false positive
